session.name: MPI-600 - Legs A/B/C run on a CORRECTED scenario; turboToggle is dead, verdict on hold pending Fabio's two repos

goal.original: Bench FLUX.2 Klein 9B - base vs turbo LoRA vs distilled vs KV - and pick the weight MPI-598 ships.
goal.summary: The S2 scenario was wrong three times over and was corrected by Fabio mid-run; every earlier S2 row is void or superseded. Legs A, B and C then ran clean - 48 rows, all six arms. Q1/Q2/Q3 answered: INT8 ships, turboToggle is dead, one checkpoint not two. Q4 (KV) is deliberately NOT answered because FluxKVCache was never in the graph. Fabio has put the verdict ON HOLD: base is not discarded, and the KV leg is re-scoped to a multi-reference edit-only speed test. Next session must also ask him for THE Ripple.

completed: S2 CORRECTED THREE TIMES by Fabio, each voiding the runs before it. (1) It ran on wf_type 5, the INPAINT branch - which green-fills the mask and depends on node 259, a flux2-klein-4b-outpaint LoRA at strength 1.1, to regenerate the fill. 4B cannot apply to 9B and the bench had bypassed it, so those runs were the branch minus the component it is built around; the surviving green was the missing LoRA, NOT a weight verdict. The localised edit is wf_type 4 WITH a mask - the mask is what makes it localised. (2) It inpainted a man from a text prompt; the ask is placing the man from IMAGE 2 (node 236) into the plate. (3) It used an ellipse; a BOX proves no-colour-shift AND correct placement at once because a straight edge shows a seam an oval hides.

The inherited 'fault 2' (wf5 hardcodes 2 steps / cfg 1 at nodes 267/254) is TRUE of branch 5 and IRRELEVANT - branch 4 samples through 185/173/170 and honours nodes 203/204 normally. The --s2-regime flag written to work around it has been deleted from sweep.py.

The inherited 'trap 1' STANDS and is fixed for good: node 52 drives MpiIfElse 57/212/222 which swap the negative between ConditioningZeroOut and the real CLIPTextEncode. sweep.py now sets it from each arm's cfg, so the blowout cannot recur by default. Re-verified by eye at the same seed - pass 1's cyan sky / neon grass became a clean correct edit.
Legs A, B and C all RUN on the corrected scenario: 48 rows in research/results.md, sectioned CURRENT / SUPERSEDED / VOID so a voided row cannot be read as a verdict.
Q1 - INT8 ships, fp8 not needed. 14.2-15.9 GB peak against 16380 MiB, FLAT across all six arms; the turbo LoRA costs nothing measurable in VRAM.

Q2 - turboToggle is DEAD. base is 6-7x slower than distilled (115 s vs 20 s whole-image edit; 192 s vs 28 s placement) AND scores 0/3 on reference placement, ignoring image 2 to copy the plate's own subject. LoRA strengths 0.7 and 0.35 score WORSE than 1.0, so no monotonic quality/speed axis exists.
Q3 - one checkpoint. base+turbo@1.0 ties distilled at 2/3 placement but needs 8 steps / 32-48 s vs 4 steps / 20-28 s, plus a second file to host and version.
research/verdict.md written, carrying a STATUS banner marking the recommendation PROVISIONAL.
A FOURTH fault was in the instrument itself: the guard's green test required r<80 and scored a visibly half-green frame at 0.00%. It now tests green dominance (g - max(r,b) > 60).
pending: THE KV SPEED LEG, re-scoped by Fabio. Install/enable FluxKVCache on the bench, KV arm ONLY, and keep it off the t2i path. Shape: EDIT ONLY (wf_type 4, NO mask - the localised edit is finished and is not part of this), with MULTIPLE references. Three images - an empty background plate plus two different people - placing BOTH people into the plate. distilled vs kv, a few runs. A single-reference test is not worth running: KV caches REFERENCE tokens, so the speedup scales with reference count.

ASK FABIO FOR 'THE Ripple'. He found two repos - an inpainting approach for Klein 9B, unproven, but on the repo's own claims broadly applicable across the app. Ask for them by that name, read them, then revisit the weight decision.
base is NOT discarded and must stay a candidate until those repos are reviewed.
Once KV and the repos land: finalise research/verdict.md, post it onto MPI-598 as an event + brief section, and close this card.

constraints: NEVER route a 9B arm through wf_type 5. That branch depends on node 259, a flux2-klein-4b-outpaint LoRA at strength 1.1, which cannot apply to a 9B base and is bypassed in this bench. Its green fill surviving is that missing LoRA, not a model failure. The localised edit is wf_type 4 WITH a mask.

A NUMBER CANNOT CLOSE THE PLACEMENT AXIS. The guard column reads green 0.00% / clip ~0.1% on ALL 18 S2 rows, including the nine where the arm placed the wrong person or nothing at all, and seam.py's worst numbers sit on runs that SUCCEEDED. Build a contact sheet (research/S2_contact_sheet.png is the pattern - crop the mask region, tile arms x seeds) and score by eye.

USE flux-2-klein-base-9b-int8-convrot-comfy.safetensors for any base arm. The originally downloaded base weight cannot be loaded by native ComfyUI at all - its comfy_quant markers omit the 'format' key.

The filenames lie: distilled and KV are {'format':'int8_tensorwise'} with SCALAR weight_scale - plain tensorwise INT8, NOT ConvRot. Only the base arm is genuinely ConvRot. Record the quantisation confound on any base-vs-distilled row.
A VRAM READING IS A LIE UNLESS YOU FREE THE BENCH FIRST - POST /free {'unload_models':true,'free_memory':true}, sample the floor, then run. sweep.py already does this before every run.

The bench is EXACTLY reproducible - same seed + same graph reproduced a byte-identical PNG across two separate invocations. So a repeat run can also come back execution_cached and hand you the PREVIOUS output file; check the filename counter before banking a 'second' measurement.
Bench is :8188, the app engine is :48188 - never drive :3000, which is Fabio's live app.
The Bash tool now BLOCKS heredocs and backslash-newline continuations on this box (backslash halving). Write python to the scratchpad with the Write tool and run it by path.
Do not use AskUserQuestion pickers with Fabio - state the assumption and proceed.
